articles.headline: AI stocks fall after hot inflation report lifts rate-hike bets
articles.summary: The selloff hit semiconductor makers, cloud providers, and other AI infrastructure names, showing how macro conditions can quickly raise the cost of capital for data-center and AI expansion plans. For business leaders, this is a sign that AI infrastructure spending may face tighter financing and more volatile supplier pricing.

articles.headline: Hyperscale cloud capex seen surging as AI server demand accelerates
articles.summary: TrendForce said combined capex from nine leading cloud service providers could reach US$957 billion in 2026 and exceed US$1.5 trillion in 2027, reflecting a major expansion in AI infrastructure budgets. That points to continued demand for servers, networking, chips, and memory, while also signaling stronger spending pressure on customers and suppliers across the cloud stack.

articles.headline: Gartner warns most neoclouds may not survive as AI infrastructure costs outpace revenue
articles.summary: TechTarget reported Gartner's view that up to 80% of neoclouds could cease independent operations by 2030 because projected AI infrastructure costs exceed revenue. For enterprises buying AI compute, this raises counterparty, continuity, and pricing-risk concerns when choosing infrastructure vendors.
